authored_scope: Random generation covers: square tiles with sides 3..5, plus about 25% non-square rectangular tiles with sides 3..5 (a synthetic extension); 2-3 tile colours; symmetric or arbitrary tiles, optionally with interior background holes; random stencil masks with sides 2..6 that touch all four sides of their box, have at least one hole and may be disconnected; vertical or horizontal separated layouts; grids 10..22 per side by default, or any caller size 1..30 that fits; and any background colour. Explicit latent arguments reconstruct the fixtures and also allow full masks, 1-wide masks and arbitrary rectangular tiles. Deliberately not supported: tiles touching the stencil, tiles whose ring contains background, multicolour stencils, multiple tiles, and outputs larger than 30x30.
authored_constraints: The tile ring is entirely non-background, so the tile forms one connected multicolour object, and its bounding box is recovered exactly.
The tile uses at least 2 non-background colours. The stencil uses exactly 1 colour, so the tile has the most distinct colours.
The stencil colour differs from the background and from every tile colour.
The tile box and stencil box are separated by at least one full background row or column, so there is no diagonal contact.
The stencil mask touches all four sides of its bounding box, so the mask equals the box contents.
The background strictly outnumbers each other colour.
Output dimensions sh*th and sw*tw are at most 30.
Numeric controls must be non-bool integers within range. Partial placement arguments are rejected.

original_audit.rule: The input has a uniform background, one multicoloured rectangular tile whose border ring is fully non-background, and one single-colour stencil that may be disconnected. The output measures (stencil bbox height x tile height) by (stencil bbox width x tile width) and starts as background. The tile is copied unchanged into block (r, c) wherever the stencil bbox mask is set. The stencil colour never appears in the output.

findings.location: generate(): the output-size guard `if tile is not None and mask is not None: if len(mask) * len(tile) > 30 ...` and the main loop where `t = _make_tile(rth, rtw, ...)` is used with `m = mask`
findings.issue: The 30x30 output bound is only checked when both tile and mask are explicit. If an explicit mask is given with a random tile, nothing limits len(mask)*th or len(mask[0])*tw. _layout_options only bounds the input layout (th+sh+1, max(tw,sw), tw+sw+1). Example: mask=[[1,1]]*11 passes _check_mask. A vertical layout fits (nh <= 17, nw <= 5). The random tile has th >= 3, so `common.grid(sw*tw, sh*th, bg)` always yields an output with at least 33 rows. A 7-row mask gives 35 rows whenever th = 5. This contradicts the docstring claim 'The output is at most 30x30'.
findings.suggested_fix: When the tile is random and the mask is explicit, draw the tile shape only from sides <= min(5, 30 // len(mask)) and <= min(5, 30 // len(mask[0])). Reject up front with ValueError if 30 // len(mask) < 3 or 30 // len(mask[0]) < 3. As a safety net, assert len(output) <= 30 and len(output[0]) <= 30 before returning.
findings.test: generate(mask=[[1,1]]*11) should raise ValueError. Currently it returns an output with >= 33 rows. Invariant for every successful call: len(out['output']) <= 30 and len(out['output'][0]) <= 30.

findings.location: _check_tile(): only checks the ring and `len(set(non-bg colours)) >= 2`. It does not check 8-connectivity of the tile's non-background cells.
findings.issue: The reference transform finds the tile as the diagonally connected multicolour object with the most distinct colours, breaking ties by size. An explicit tile can have a single-colour ring and an interior non-background island separated from the ring by background. Example: a 7x7 tile with a ring of 5, a background ring at offset 1, and a 3x3 core of 6/7, on bg 0. The core then has 2 colours and the ring has 1, so the transform crops only the 3x3 core. It then treats the ring cells as stencil cells, which changes both the stencil bbox and the output. A 5x5 version also fails: ring 5, interior bg except a centre of 7, and a near-full 6x6 mask. All objects have one colour, and the stencil component (35 cells) outranks the ring (16 cells), so the stencil is taken as the tile. The generator accepts both scenes and emits outputs that disagree with the reference.
findings.suggested_fix: In _check_tile, require all non-background tile cells to form a single 8-connected component, and require that component to contain >= 2 colours. Apply the same predicate as an acceptance test inside _make_tile.

findings.location: _make_tile(): the acceptance condition `if len(used) >= 2: return tile` for 5x5 tiles
findings.issue: In random generation a 5x5 tile can have a monochrome ring, keys (1,1)/(1,2)/(2,1) set to background, and a differently coloured centre (2,2). The centre is then an isolated 1-cell object. The tile still passes the used-colour check. A random 6x6 mask (allowed since 30//5 = 6) with density up to 0.75 can contain a single-colour component larger than 16 cells. The reference transform would then select the stencil component over the 16-cell ring. Equal sizes of 16 depend on max() ordering. By hand estimate this affects roughly 0.1% of tiles, so it needs execution to measure.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the same connected-component predicate as the explicit path, and redraw the tile when it fails.
findings.test: Generate about 5000 scenes with generate(background=0) and run the reference transform on each. Count mismatches. Also assert that every tile has non-background cells forming one 8-connected component with >= 2 colours.

findings.issue: The docstring says an explicit tile 'may be any rectangle whose ring is non-background'. This is too broad, because the transform's tile identification depends on connectivity and the colour count of the connected object, as shown above. Explicit tiles of side 1 or 2, such as [[1,2]], are also accepted. These are fine for the transform but undocumented.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the connectivity requirement and the accepted minimum sizes once the connectivity check is added.
findings.test: generate(width=10, height=10, background=0, tile=[[1,2]], mask=[[1,0,1]], stencil_color=3) should succeed with a 1x6 output equal to [1,2,0,0,1,2].

findings.issue: Random stencils always have both sides >= 2 and at least one hole. Random tiles are 3..5 per side, and stencils are always vertically or horizontally separated from the tile. One-row stencils, full stencils and degenerate tiles are reachable only through explicit arguments. These limits are declared, but they limit diversity.
findings.suggested_fix: None required. Optionally sample a 1xN stencil with low probability.
findings.test: Over 1000 random calls, confirm that the stencil bbox dims fall in 2..6 and that both orientations ('v' and 'h') occur.

targeted_checks: Reconstructed the fixtures by hand from validate() arguments. All four masks match the input stencil cells. Tile positions, grid sizes, the separation gaps and the output dimensions (9x12, 12x9, 12x12, 25x25) are consistent with the canonical data.
_place: extra = side - th - sh >= 1 is guaranteed by the nh/nw filter, so randint(1, extra) is safe and the separation gap is >= 1.
The _gap predicate a1 + 1 < b0 enforces at least one full background line, so the stencil cells never fall inside the tile bbox.
Booleans are rejected for width, height, colours, placements, mask values and tile cells via _is_int.
Partial placement arguments are rejected before any other placement checks.
Background dominance is a strict plurality check and matches a mode-based background() in the transform.
Random tile palettes exclude the stencil colour, so the stencil and tile colours never collide.
scope_limits: No code was executed. The frequency of the random-path 5x5 isolated-centre defect is estimated by hand.
